# generate-release-summary

Lets [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli-in-actions) draft the summary of a release for the release notes, from the commits of the release.
The summary is written for the users of the project: what is new, improved, or fixed, and what they have to do, in about 120 words.

A summary is a nice to have: **when it cannot be generated, the action warns and succeeds without a summary**, so a release is never held up by it.
Check the summary before you rely on it, it is generated by a language model.

## Usage

```yaml
jobs:
  release-summary:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      copilot-requests: write # is needed by Copilot CLI to bill its requests to the organization
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@...
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # the commits since the previous release are summarized
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: philips-software/amp-devcontainer/.github/actions/generate-release-summary@...
        id: summary
        with:
          release-tag: ${{ github.ref_name }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@...
        if: ${{ steps.summary.outputs.generated == 'true' }}
        with:
          name: release-summary
          path: ${{ steps.summary.outputs.summary-file }}
```

The summary is meant to be passed to [render-release-notes](../render-release-notes/README.md) as `summary-file`, which makes it available to the template as `release.summary`.
Do this from another job, the job above does not need, and should not have, permission to change the release.

### Prerequisites

Copilot CLI authenticates with the `GITHUB_TOKEN` of the workflow, there is no personal access token or secret to manage.

- The workflow must run in an organization-owned repository, and the organization must have Copilot CLI turned on.
- An organization owner must enable the policy *Allow use of Copilot CLI billed to the organization*. The usage is then billed to the organization, not to a person.
- The job needs the `copilot-requests: write` permission. It is a scope that [actionlint](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) does not know yet.
- Usage is not limited by user budgets. To limit the spending, use a cost center with a budget, see [Copilot CLI in GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agent-capabilities/agent-powered-workflows-and-operations/copilot-cli-in-github-actions).

The action installs Node.js and a pinned version of `@github/copilot` (see [package.json](./package.json), updated by Dependabot).

## Inputs and outputs

| Name           | Kind   | Description                                                                                                                                                |
|----------------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `release-tag`  | input  | Tag of the release to summarize. The repository must be checked out with all tags and history. Required.                                                   |
| `tag-pattern`  | input  | Pattern (see `git describe --match`) of the tags of earlier releases. The commits since the latest tag that matches are summarized. Defaults to `v[0-9]*`. |
| `output-file`  | input  | Path the summary is written to. Defaults to `release-summary.md`.                                                                                          |
| `github-token` | input  | Token Copilot authenticates with. Defaults to the workflow token.                                                                                          |
| `generated`    | output | `true` when a summary was generated, `false` when it was not.                                                                                              |
| `summary-file` | output | Path to the summary, empty when there is none.                                                                                                             |

At most the latest 200 commits are summarized, at most 20000 characters of commit subjects are given to Copilot, and the summary is limited to 1500 characters.
For the first release, without an earlier tag, these are the latest commits of the history.

## How it works

- Copilot is started with `--model auto`, so GitHub picks the model for the task.
- It is given the subjects of the commits as data, between markers that can't be guessed, with the instruction to ignore any instruction in them. It has no tools to look at changes in more detail: even read-only git commands can write files (for example with `--output`), which would let a commit message change what runs afterwards with the token available.
- It can't run commands, write files, fetch URLs, or remember anything, its built-in GitHub tools and the custom instructions of the repository are turned off, and the token is redacted from its output.
- The text it returns is [sanitized](./sanitize.py) before it is used: HTML and comments (that could contain the markers of the release notes), images (also the ones that use a reference), links to other places than GitHub, and at-mentions are removed or defused, and it is shortened at a line boundary. A code block that is open at the end, for example because the text was shortened, is closed with a fence like the one that opened it.
- Generating the summary takes at most five minutes.

Commits can contain text from contributors, so a prompt injection can't be ruled out. The measures above make sure that the worst that can happen is a poor summary: Copilot can't change anything, and the job has a read-only token.
The summary has no effect on what is released, and is marked in the release notes as drafted by Copilot.

## Failures

The action succeeds without a summary (`generated` is `false`, a warning is shown) when:

- the tag is not found, or there are no commits to summarize;
- Copilot is not installed, is not allowed to be used, returns an error, or does not finish in time;
- nothing is left of the summary after sanitizing it.

Only a missing `release-tag` fails the action, as that is a mistake in the workflow.

## Tests

The tests use a generated repository with fake releases, and a fake Copilot CLI that records how it is called. They need Bats, Git and python3, which the amp-devcontainer-docs image provides. Run them from the repository root:

```bash
bats .github/actions/generate-release-summary/test
```
